builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Masked Diffusion Language Agents for Tool-Integrated Chemical Reasoning
summary: It replaces autoregressive left-to-right generation in tool-using agents with iterative masked-diffusion denoising over interleaved reasoning and tool-call trajectories, so tool decisions are conditioned on full-trajectory bidirectional context rather than only the past. The cost is a non-standard masked-diffusion model plus a two-stage post-training pipeline (agentic supervised fine-tuning and variance-reduced preference optimization), iterative multi-step denoising at inference, and tooling for diffusion-LM serving that is far less mature than the autoregressive stack. It can fail because the reported gains hold only on the authors' chemistry benchmark under matched budgets and may not transfer to other domains, and arbitrary-order decoding offers little benefit on strictly sequential tasks while the absence of optimized KV-cache and batching support can erode the quality advantage in latency and serving complexity.
rationale: The method depends on a masked-diffusion language model and a domain-specific post-training pipeline whose benefits are demonstrated only on a chemistry benchmark, so its production value for a small team with one GPU is unproven outside that setting.
technique: Masked diffusion tool-integrated chemical reasoning agent

claims.statement: It replaces autoregressive left-to-right generation in tool-using agents with iterative masked-diffusion denoising over interleaved reasoning and tool-call trajectories, so tool decisions are conditioned on full-trajectory bidirectional context rather than only the past. The cost is a non-standard masked-diffusion model plus a two-stage post-training pipeline (agentic supervised fine-tuning and variance-reduced preference optimization), iterative multi-step denoising at inference, and tooling for diffusion-LM serving that is far less mature than the autoregressive stack. It can fail because the reported gains hold only on the authors' chemistry benchmark under matched budgets and may not transfer to other domains, and arbitrary-order decoding offers little benefit on strictly sequential tasks while the absence of optimized KV-cache and batching support can erode the quality advantage in latency and serving complexity.

Approximately 20% overall improvement over autoregressive agents under matched budgets and evaluation on a six-task chemistry benchmark; the 8B model is reported as comparable to, and in some cases surpassing, GPT 5.5 and Claude Opus 4.7.
